title: President Trump modifies Canadian products subject to Section 338 tariffs
excerpt: The changes to the tariff list, which take effect on October 30, 2026, remove certain goods while adding valves, carpets, and waste products.
bodyHtml:
On October 23, 2026, the White House announced that President Donald J. Trump signed a Proclamation to modify the scope of tariffs on Canadian products under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930.

These tariffs apply to covered goods regardless of their origin under the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement and are in addition to duties imposed under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962.

The modification removes plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery, refrigeration equipment, and specific packing crates and boxes from the tariff list. These items are being replaced with certain valves, carpets, waste products, and other goods.

The adjustments to the product list are scheduled to take effect on October 30, 2026. Section 338 authorizes the President to suspend, revoke, supplement, or amend any proclamation under Section 338 whenever the President deems that the public interests require such action.
topic: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Further Modifies Canadian Products Subject to Tariffs Under Section 338
